title: Ottawa ankle rules (adult)
anchor: inability to weight bear (four steps) immediately after the injury and in the emergency department.

clauses.text: For traumatic ankle pain, the guidance recommends radiography when any ankle criterion below is present.
The ankle tenderness criteria are point tenderness at the posterior edge of the distal 6 cm or tip of either the lateral or medial malleolus.
The weight-bearing criterion is inability to take four steps both immediately after injury AND at emergency-department assessment.
For traumatic midfoot pain, imaging criteria are tenderness at the fifth-metatarsal base or navicular, or the same inability to take four steps at both times.

applicability: This is an adult clinical imaging rule. The relevant pain region and examination findings must be established.
limitations: Walking now does not establish every criterion. A message cannot supply an unreported bony examination. The source does not specify telehealth routing or make every incomplete rule an emergency.

title: Sprains and strains
anchor: Most can be treated at home without seeing a GP.

clauses.text: For sprains and strains, the page describes initial protection, rest, ice, compression and elevation, followed by movement as pain permits.
It advises urgent assessment for severe or worsening pain or swelling, inability to bear weight or walk more than a few steps, marked stiffness, lack of improvement, or fever/shivering.
It advises emergency assessment after an injury with a heard crack, deformity, numbness/tingling, or blue/grey/cold skin.

applicability: Home treatment assumes a suitable uncomplicated injury; the escalation qualifications remain part of this card.
limitations: This UK public guidance does not establish that a particular injury is a sprain, exclude fracture, or validate remote examination. Service names and contact arrangements are jurisdiction-specific. Medication suitability requires separate assessment.

title: Insomnia — Diagnosis
publisher: National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute
anchor: If not getting enough sleep is affecting your daily activities, talk to your doctor.

clauses.text: The source recommends clinician contact when insufficient sleep affects daily activities.
Its chronic-insomnia description requires symptoms on at least three nights each week for at least three months.
Evaluation considers sleep pattern, duration, daytime function, health and medication history, substance use, and possible other sleep disorders; examination or testing may be needed.

applicability: Daytime impact and frequency must be established from the current person’s history, not inferred from source descriptions.
limitations: The diagnostic duration criterion is not a minimum waiting time before seeking assessment. This page does not assign urgency or a care channel. A short sleep complaint alone does not establish chronic insomnia.

title: FDA recommends avoiding NSAIDs in pregnancy at 20 weeks or later
anchor: The above recommendations do not apply to low-dose 81 mg aspirin prescribed for certain conditions in pregnancy.

clauses.text: Avoid NSAID use at 20 weeks of pregnancy or later unless specifically advised by a healthcare professional; fetal kidney problems and low amniotic fluid are the concern. Check combination OTC products for NSAIDs.

If necessary between 20 and 30 weeks, clinician-directed treatment should use the lowest effective dose for the shortest duration; consider amniotic-fluid monitoring beyond 48 hours. Avoid use at 30 weeks and later because of additional fetal cardiac risk.
The warning excludes NSAIDs administered directly to the eye and prescribed low-dose 81 mg aspirin for certain pregnancy-related conditions. It is not advice to stop such prescribed aspirin.

applicability: Identify the actual medication, gestational age and existing clinician instructions.
limitations: This medication warning does not diagnose injury, establish that exposure occurred, assign a care setting, or imply that every exposure caused harm.

title: Diabetic Foot
anchor: Serious foot problems can develop quickly.

clauses.text: For a person with diabetes, the page advises prompt clinician assessment for a foot cut, blister or bruise not beginning to heal after a few days; red, warm or painful foot skin; blood in a callus; or black, foul-smelling infection.
Preventive measures include daily inspection, protecting skin and routine foot checks. Nerve damage may reduce sensation, so limited pain does not establish absence of injury.

applicability: The current person must have diabetes and the relevant foot finding; general risk factors are not observed patient facts.
limitations: The page does not define a remote-service response guarantee, prove infection or gangrene, or establish that asynchronous review completes the required examination.

title: Signs and Symptoms of Tuberculosis
publisher: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
anchor: Contact your health care provider or local health department and ask about TB testing.

clauses.text: Active pulmonary TB may cause cough lasting at least three weeks, chest pain or coughing up blood/sputum. Other symptoms can include weight loss, fatigue, fever and night sweats.
For symptoms of active TB, the page advises contacting a healthcare provider or local health department about testing.
Inactive or latent TB does not cause active-disease symptoms and is not contagious, although untreated infection can later become active.

applicability: Symptoms have multiple causes. The page does not establish TB from a message or classify an untested person as latent rather than active.
limitations: No remote assessment deadline, safe waiting interval or individual infection-control clearance is supplied by this page.

title: Pulmonary Embolism
anchor: It can be difficult to diagnose PE.

clauses.text: Possible PE symptoms include breathlessness, rapid breathing or heart rate, chest discomfort worsened by deep breath or coughing, coughing blood, lightheadedness or fainting. PE can be life-threatening.
Diagnosis uses clinical history, risk factors and examination, commonly with imaging and blood testing.
A person who has PE needs treatment promptly; the source describes medication and procedural treatment options.

applicability: Symptoms are not specific for PE. A message neither confirms PE nor completes its exclusion.
limitations: The treatment statement concerns PE, not a diagnosis inferred solely from chest pain. This page does not authorize remote rule-out, guarantee safe delay, or establish a service-specific triage threshold.
